A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GENIE. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, equations, and figures support comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting. Internal reporting inconsistencies limit particular interpretations but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on watermark verification, link-prediction utility, embedding baselines, watermark removal, and ownership piracy, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity simulations, additional attacks, pretrained-model experiments, and inductive and heterophily evaluations.

M1.justification: The core link-inversion triggers and alternating clean/watermark training updates remain. The stated registration procedure changes: v2 Section 4.4 publishes Dwm on the public bulletin board, whereas v4 Appendix D and Algorithm 4 publish its cryptographic hash, preserving the trigger's secrecy.

E1.justification: v4 adds inductive link prediction on Wikipedia and PubMed with LEAP, plus seven additional attributed-graph benchmarks used to investigate heterophily (Table 43). Router, ogbl-collab, and the earlier transductive Wikipedia evaluation are retained from v2 Appendix D, rather than newly added.

E2.justification: v4 Table 3 adds four evaluated comparators: Link-Backdoor, Effective Backdoor, Erdos-Renyi Induced Watermark, and Erdos-Renyi Inject Watermark. The original Xu fine-tuning, Adi data-poisoning, uniform-loss, and MGDA embedding comparison remains in v4 Table 4; it was not replaced by these new baselines.

E3.justification: New settings include pretrained GCN initialization, GAT/GIN and LEAP evaluations, 80% feature masking, and watermark-rate and distribution sweeps. The original 80/10/10 split and 50/400-epoch budgets remain. v4 Algorithm 1 specifies normally distributed watermark vectors where v2 specified uniform sampling; this is a reported specification change, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds pretrained-model ablation, watermark-rate and vector-distribution sensitivity tests, DWT sample-size/bandwidth sensitivity, and homophily characterization. Robustness testing adds randomized feature subsampling and six combination attacks. The existing adaptive-query defense, piracy trajectories, and most detailed fine-pruning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The original ten-run averages and bootstrap-test results remain. v4 adds confidence-controlled DWT block sampling and reports threshold means and standard deviations over 1,000 Monte Carlo trials in Tables 14–15. Appendix B discusses multiple-comparison correction without reporting adjusted p-values; it does not establish that correction was applied.

E6.justification: The main performance table is unchanged (v2 Table 4; v4 Table 2), but v4 adds extensive baseline, architecture, inductive, heterophily, sensitivity, and attack results. For example, new PPI feature-subsampling results report 24.3% watermark AUC and 89.8% test AUC. Extraction results are consolidated without fully retaining the earlier architecture distinctions, preventing reliable same-setting performance comparisons. The 100% pruning controls are omitted.

T1.justification: v4 adds a DWT binomial confidence theorem and its derivation in Appendix C.2, explicit independence and distributional assumptions, and KDE error reasoning. Appendix E supplies time and space complexity derivations for both watermark-generation procedures. These substantially extend v2's largely informal statistical assurance.

C1.justification: The first-LP-watermarking, utility-preservation, and robustness contributions remain. The DWT contribution is reformulated from an FPR/FNR assurance below 10^-6 to a misclassification bound at specified confidence under stated assumptions. The conclusion explicitly qualifies inductive evaluation as preliminary and leaves dynamic or temporal networks open.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly discusses failure if watermark features become accessible, distinguishes transductive and inductive threat assumptions, and identifies temporal evolution as an unresolved limitation. It adds interpretations concerning feature homophily, attention-based regularization, and quadratic generation costs. These substantially expand the applicability and mechanism discussion beyond v2.

D1.justification: v4 adds code/artifact access information, a DWT calculator reference, four pseudocode algorithms, baseline-construction details, and watermark-rate selection criteria. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Core hardware, architecture, learning-rate, and training-budget disclosures are retained; some extraction-setting distinctions and the original explicit bootstrap-resample count are no longer documented.

R1.justification: v4 expands positioning through direct evaluation of previously discussed LP backdoors and adapted graph-watermarking methods. New literature connects GENIE to inductive LP, heterophily, expressive GNN architectures, and binomial/KDE theory, while several general background references are removed. The central novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, threat model, and evaluation narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Ownership demonstration and detailed attack descriptions move to appendices, the original embedding comparison becomes an ablation section, and model/metric notation is simplified. These are substantial organizational and language changes beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a single-column layout, redraws the conceptual and system-overview figures, and consolidates attack results into a paired heatmap. The original standalone subgraph-generation and DWT density illustrations disappear. Tables are reorganized, failure markings change to strikethroughs, and numerous new tables and algorithm displays are introduced.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects v2's instruction to publish the secret watermark by specifying hash registration, adds missing whole-scheme baseline comparisons, and supplies focused robustness and sensitivity evidence. Explicit DWT assumptions and clearer applicability limits further strengthen the paper. Numerical disagreements between Figure 3 and Section 5.4.3 weaken reporting reliability, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in security coherence and evidential support.
